bar: Q3 FY27 revenue: company guide $115.0-124.0M (midpoint $119.5M), Ambarella Q2 FY27 release 2026-09-03 https://finviz.com/news/388851/ambarella-inc-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results ; consensus $119.44M (Investing.com, 2026-11-24 https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ambarella-earnings-on-deck-as-ai-chip-transition-faces-test-93CH-5048515), $119.8M (Benzinga) and $119.9M (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16 https://finviz.com/news/423396/ambarellas-physical-ai-pitch-meets-a-margin-inventory-and-memory-test). Several sources agree on revenue, so the bar is sourced. Non-GAAP EPS disagrees: $0.31 (Investing), $0.32 (EW, whisper $0.37) and $0.22 in one snippet, so EPS is not used as the bar. Q4 FY27 (Jan-27 quarter) revenue consensus is $112.6M from 11 analysts (range $109.35-116.75M), per Yahoo analysis https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMBA/analysis/ and Benzinga. FY26 revenue was $390M; the company's original FY27 frame was +10-15% (= $429-449M).
positioning_check: Short interest is about 10.5% of float at about 2.6 days to cover (Equibles, latest settlement, page dated around 2026-11-13, https://equibles.com/stocks/amba/short-interest). Other readings: 5.15M shares and 3.5 days as of 2026-09-30 (massive.com); 5.15M shares and 3.1 days on a page dated 2026-10-23 (shortsqueeze.com). That is moderate and not a crowded short. The 25-delta skew is -6.92 vol points, so calls are paid over puts ('upside paid'). Put/call open interest is 0.23 on total OI of only 4,044, so the market is leaning to upside, plausibly the takeover tail. The ATM straddle is wide (52% of mid), so the 12.67% event move is indicative only. Tape: -27.2% over 20 days, -8.75% over 5 days, 0.4% above the 52-week low, and down about 10-12% today (from a $55.56 Monday close to $48.86 at the seal) on a semis selloff and a Morgan Stanley target cut.

findings.finding: On the Q2 FY27 call (2026-09-03/04) management did NOT re-confirm the +10-15% FY27 revenue frame (it came from an analyst's question). The CEO said 'the outcome this year is still a little uncertain' because of memory constraints, and that Q4 should show 'regular seasonality' barring memory impact. Memory supply is the named swing factor for the Q4 guide being given tonight. Regular seasonality off the Q3 midpoint is the FY26 Q3-to-Q4 step of -8% ($108.5M to $100.1M), which gives about $110M. That sits below the $112.6M Q4 consensus. Any memory haircut on top lands the guide further under it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The name has fallen after 6 of its last 7 prints (-0.8, -21.4, -14.9, -18.8, +16.8, -15.1, -17.1). The Q3 FY26 print (2025-11-25) beat and fell 18.8% on the guide/outlook. After the last print the stock fell (AllInvestView cites -6.3% on the seasonal Q3 outlook and memory/supply-chain costs; the baseline reads -0.8% close-to-close).
findings.why_not_priced: Q4 consensus of $112.6M (Yahoo/Benzinga) sits above the seasonal arithmetic. If the street had priced a memory-constrained Q4, that consensus would sit at or below $110M and the estimates would have moved down. Investing.com says estimates were flat over 60 days. Part of it is plausibly in today's -12% and the 27% 20-day slide, which is why this is sized below the implied move.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-16) separately flags memory as the stated uncertainty, but it reads the same call, so it is the same document. Arlo (a camera OEM) flagged a constrained memory market and memory cost risk on its Q3 2026 call: https://finviz.com/news/418098/arlo-tops-consensus-but-misses-the-whisper-as-slowing-arr-growth-collides-with-a-bold-2027-target

findings.finding: Peer Himax (2026-11-05) guided Q4 revenue down 22-26% sequentially on an abrupt China-driven correction in automotive driver-IC orders. Chinese customers cut Q4 forecasts after the early-October National Day holiday, citing overly aggressive export expectations and channel inventory. The stock fell more than 20%. Ambarella's auto business set a record in Q2 FY27 and includes in-cabin wins at Chinese Tier-1s, so the same Chinese auto channel could trim its Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history on a peer read-through for AMBA. Auto is about 22% of FY26 revenue, and its Q2 FY27 strength came from commercial-vehicle AI rather than Chinese passenger cars.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer (display drivers), not a counterparty, and Ambarella has not spoken since. If the read-through were priced, AMBA's Q4 auto expectations would have been cut. Q4 consensus was flat over 60 days per Investing.com.
findings.independence: Proxy only. A different product (display driver vs. vision SoC), and Ambarella's auto mix is mostly commercial-vehicle telematics and safety rather than Chinese passenger cars, so the rest of the auto segment (and the 78% that is IoT) may offset it. No direct AMBA counterparty confirmation found.

findings.finding: Camera OEMs pre-bought components through 2026 as memory tightened. Hikvision's inventory rose to CNY 33.3bn at end-September from CNY 20.5bn at end-2025 (+63%), and 9-month operating cash flow fell 47% on higher purchases. Dahua's inventory rose 41% in H1. Ambarella's Q3 guide of +11% QoQ, its own inventory build ($52.2M to $76.9M Jan-Jul; days of inventory 157 vs 76 a year earlier) and the camera-chain stockpiling point to pull-forward and a risk of Q4 digestion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history on a channel-inventory read for AMBA. Last year's Q3 beat was followed by -18.8% on the outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: Chinese-language and German coverage of a non-customer's balance sheet. If the US street had priced camera-chain pull-forward into AMBA, its Q4 consensus would sit below seasonal rather than above it.
findings.independence: Hikvision is not a disclosed AMBA customer, so this is an industry proxy. The AMBA inventory figures are from AMBA's own Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/388851/ambarella-inc-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results), and days of inventory are from the Earnings Whispers preview, a different source.

findings.finding: Takeover tail: the FT reported on 2026-07-31 that NXP is in talks to buy Ambarella (stock +18-19%). A secondary outlet reported exclusive, non-binding talks with NXP after the board weighed offers (Qualcomm and Nvidia reported as bidders) on 2026-10-30/31. Betaville chatter on 2026-11-19 said the deal 'may be in final stages', with trader talk of $95-100 a share (stock +9% to about $59.75 intraday). The stock now sits at $48.86, about half that talk and at its 52-week low. Management will be asked on tonight's call. An announcement, or anything short of a denial, is a large upside path; confirmation that talks ended is a downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FT report moved the stock +18-19% (2026-07-31). The Betaville chatter moved it about +9-12% intraday (2026-11-19), all of which was given back within three sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: At $48.86 against $95-100 talk the market is assigning a low probability. If a deal were priced, the stock would trade well above its pre-FT level rather than at a 52-week low. Newsquawk calls Betaville chatter low-reliability, and nothing is confirmed by either company. Calls being bid (skew -6.9, P/C OI 0.23) is the market's own small lean toward this tail.
findings.independence: FT original via Investing.com, 2026-07-31: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ambarella-reportedly-in-talks-to-be-acquired-by-nxp-semiconductors-shares-spike-4829078 ; exclusive-talks report, 2026-10-31: https://cryptobriefing.com/ambarella-exclusive-talks-nxp-acquisition/ (single secondary outlet, unnamed source). These are three different reports of one thread; none is from the companies.

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (a memory-constrained Q4 guide below the $112.6M consensus) cuts against the skew (-6.9, calls paid) and against a stock already down 27% in 20 days and about 12% today. The negatives are sized below the implied move and p_up is held near 50 (47) for that reason, with the takeover tail as the explicit reason the option market leans up.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning): the memory/Q4-guide negative runs against a -6.9 call skew; short interest (about 10.5% of float, 2.6-3.1 days) is moderate, not crowded. Shrunk -3.0 to -2.5 and moved p_up from 45 to 47.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the Himax read-through is an unlinked peer in a different product, so it was shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0. The Hikvision inventory proxy was shrunk from -1.0 to -0.8. Both stay filed.
Lessons 1 and 6 (inside the guide; beats sold): the Q3 reported-quarter base case lands inside the company guide on a name that sells beats. Moved from +0.5 to 0.
Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue bar is sourced to the company guide and three agreeing estimates. EPS sources disagree, so EPS is not used as a bar and no cap was needed.

Left standing: the M&A tail (+2.0, 'other', sourced to three reports of one thread), the positioning reset (+2.0), the gross-margin and cash-conversion items (-0.5 each), Arlo (+0.3) and insider sales (-0.2).
